cases.description: Northside Electric Co-op. Monthly bill for residential electric service at her apartment.
cases.basis: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists electricity.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Electricity is listed as shelter, so if someone else pays her electric bill directly, it counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Electricity for her home is on the manual's list of shelter costs, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Gas service for the home is listed as shelter, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Gas service for the home is on the manual's list of shelter costs, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Propane delivered to heat her home is heating fuel, which the manual lists as a shelter cost.

regs.reason: Shelter. Water and sewer service are named in the rules as shelter costs, so someone else paying this bill counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Water and sewer service are both on the manual's list of shelter items, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.

cases.description: Valley Waste Services. Curbside garbage pickup at her home, monthly.
cases.basis: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists garbage collection services.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. The rules list garbage collection as shelter, so when someone else pays this bill it counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Garbage pickup at her home is on the manual's list of shelter items, so a third party paying it counts as in-kind support.

cases.description: Maple Court Apartments. December rent for her apartment, unit 4B.
cases.basis: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists rent.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Rent is listed as shelter, so paying her apartment rent for her counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Rent is listed as shelter, so if someone else pays it to the landlord, it counts as in-kind support.

cases.description: First Home Mortgage. Monthly mortgage payment on the house she owns.
cases.basis: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists mortgage payments.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. When someone else pays her mortgage directly to the lender, the rules treat it as in-kind support for housing.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. A mortgage payment on the home she lives in counts as shelter, so someone else paying it counts as in-kind support.

cases.description: Brookfield County Treasurer. Real property tax installment on her home.
cases.basis: 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) lists real property taxes.

regs.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. The rules list real property taxes as shelter, so someone else paying her home's property tax counts as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Yes, this is a shelter cost. Real property taxes on her home are listed as a shelter item, so someone else paying them counts as in-kind support.

cases.description: Horizon Wireless. Monthly cell phone plan in her name.
cases.basis: POMS SI 00815.400B.2: a sister paying the phone bill does not result in income.

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. A cell phone plan isn't on the list of housing costs, so someone else paying it shouldn't count as shelter support.

poms.reason: Not shelter. Phone service isn't food or shelter, so another person paying her cell phone bill doesn't count as in-kind support.

cases.description: FastNet. Home internet service, monthly.
cases.basis: Not in the shelter list of 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1); POMS SI 00835.465D.1 says its list of household costs is the only one used.

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. Home internet isn't on the list of housing costs that count, so someone else paying it doesn't count as housing support.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. Home internet is not on the manual's closed list of housing costs, so a family member paying it doesn't count as in-kind support.

cases.description: CableVision. Cable television package, monthly.
cases.basis: Not in the shelter list of 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) or POMS SI 00835.020B.36.

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. Cable TV isn't on the list of housing costs that count, so someone else paying it shouldn't count as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. Cable TV is not on the manual's closed list of housing costs, so a relative paying it directly does not count as in-kind support.

cases.description: FreshMart. Weekly groceries delivered to her apartment.
cases.basis: 89 FR 21199: food is no longer counted as in-kind support from September 30, 2024.

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. Groceries are food, and food no longer counts as in-kind support. Only housing costs like rent, mortgage, and utilities do.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost: groceries are food, not housing. When someone else pays the grocer, it still counts as in-kind support in the form of food.

cases.description: Northside Physical Therapy. Co-pay for a weekly therapy session.
cases.basis: Not a shelter item; not in 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1).

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. A physical therapy co-pay is a medical bill, and it isn't on the list of housing costs that count as shelter.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. A physical therapy co-pay is a medical bill, not one of the housing costs on the manual's list, so someone else paying it isn't in-kind support.

cases.description: Riverside Mobility Repair. New push rims and a brake adjustment for her wheelchair.
cases.basis: Not a shelter item; not in 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1).

regs.reason: Not shelter. A wheelchair repair isn't housing, and it isn't on the regulation's list of shelter costs, so someone else paying it doesn't count as in-kind support.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. Wheelchair repair is not rent, mortgage, property taxes, or a utility, so it is not on the manual's list of shelter costs.

cases.description: Eastgate Community College. Spring semester tuition.
cases.basis: Not a shelter item; not in 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1).

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. College tuition isn't housing, so a family member paying it directly to the college doesn't count as housing help under these rules.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. College tuition isn't on the manual's list of housing costs, so someone else paying it directly to the college isn't counted as housing support.

cases.description: SafeDrive Auto Insurance. Six-month premium for her car.
cases.basis: Not a shelter item; POMS SI 00835.465D.3 counts only property insurance required by a mortgage holder.

regs.reason: Not a shelter cost. Car insurance is not on the list of housing costs, so someone else paying it does not count as housing support.

poms.reason: Not shelter. Car insurance isn't on the list of housing costs, so a relative paying it directly doesn't count as in-kind support.

cases.description: HomeShield. Monthly renters insurance premium for her apartment.
cases.basis: POMS SI 00835.465D.3 counts only property insurance required by a mortgage holder; renters insurance is not.

regs.reason: Not shelter. Renters insurance is not on the regulations' list of shelter costs, so someone else paying it should not count as housing support.

poms.reason: Not a shelter cost. Renters insurance is chosen by the renter, and only insurance a mortgage lender requires counts as a housing cost.

cases.description: SafeKeep Self Storage. Monthly rent for a storage unit holding her furniture.
cases.basis: POMS SI 00835.020B.36: shelter is living quarters; a storage unit is not.

regs.reason: Not shelter. A storage unit holds her furniture, not her. Like the lawn-service example, someone paying it does not give her housing.

poms.reason: Not shelter. A storage unit holds her furniture but is not where she lives. Only housing costs for her living quarters count as shelter.

cases.description: Brookfield Mutual. Homeowners insurance premium on her house, required by her mortgage lender.
cases.basis: POMS SI 00835.020B.36 and SI 00835.465D.3 count property insurance required by a mortgage holder; the shelter list in 20 CFR 416.1130(b)(1) does not include insurance.

regs.reason: Unclear. Homeowners insurance is not on the shelter list, but the lender requires it, and these passages don't say whether that makes it part of the mortgage payment.

poms.reason: Yes, it's a shelter cost. Her mortgage lender requires this homeowners insurance, and that kind of insurance counts as a housing cost when someone else pays it.

cases.description: SuperLink. One bill for residential electric service and home internet together.
cases.basis: Electricity is shelter and internet is not, so a single payment for both is mixed.

regs.reason: Unclear. The electricity part is a shelter cost, but home internet is not on the shelter list. The rules don't say how to treat one bill that combines both.

poms.reason: Unclear. The electric part counts as shelter, but the internet part does not. The bill doesn't show how much each part costs, and the manual doesn't address bundled bills like this.
